title: Do choices identify reward numbers?
hook: Different reward tables can make the same predictions.

knows: A grid world: an agent moves, collects points, ends at a goal.
doesNotKnow: Exhibit distinct reward tables with equal observation likelihood under a stated ordinal choice rule.

objective: Exhibit distinct reward tables with equal observation likelihood under a stated ordinal choice rule.
misconception: A favoured action ordering identifies one true numerical reward table.

claims.text: H1 rewards2/0, H2 rewards10/9, H0 rewards0/0. Three hypotheses have equal priors; choices are independent given hypothesis.
claims.source: src/demos/ai/ai-reward-ambiguity/Demo.tsx#picture#tables; src/demos/ai/ai-reward-ambiguity/model.ts + model.test.mjs finite author implementation reproduction; https://ai.stanford.edu/~ang/papers/icml00-irl.pdf — Ng and Russell (2000), reward-identification framing; body fetched 2026-10-19. Exact equal likelihoods arise from the locally declared ordinal noise rule, not every IRL model.
